messages:
sarah: Heads-up — seeing repeated tail latency spikes in eu-west GPU pool since vision-inc rolled model v2.1 at 03:20 UTC. Spikes align with big egress bursts to S3, plus KV cache churn. Dash: https://dash.redwood/eu-west/gpu?panel=tail_latency

miguel: thx — can you paste the job id / pod? wondering if it's a single tenant hogging NIC queues or a multi-host pattern

sarah: pod/job: vision-inc-infer-7b-2026-03-21-03:20. Mostly 3 hosts but spikes correlate with one host (eu-west-1b-rack-22). 95p token latency jumps from 90ms -> 1.8s.

miguel: got it. looking at netdev stats now. early guess: NIC TX queue saturation + pcie stalls when they do batched embedding exports.

alloc-bot: Allocation event: tenant=vision-inc pool=shared-gpu-eu-west slot_count=12 -> increased to 20 at 1746788900 by autoscaler

jason: If it's that bursty, dedicated slice might be cleaner. carve out a fractional dedicated pool for them during heavy windows? avoids noisy neighbor for others.

lee: dedicated helps isolation but costs jump. rough calc: devs asked for 8 extra vGPU slices (~$9k/mo). We need threshold rule: only carve when 95p-latency > 500ms for >10m AND burst egress > 200MB/s.

anya: alternative: soft-routing + fallback to a quantized variant for their embedding export path. Reduce egress burst and CPU footprint. We can add a routing rule: if egress > X then route to model:v2-quantized.

miguel: also can try NIC queue shaping + per-tenant egress policer in the proxy to smooth peaks. Quick test: apply hf policer at 200MB/s and spin up a warm dedicated slice for canary.

sarah: @miguel can you run policer experiment on rack-22 for 30m? if it reduces 95p to <250ms we can postpone carveout.

miguel: on it. plan:
```
# on host eu-west-1b-rack-22
sudo tc qdisc add dev eth0 root tbf rate 200mbit burst 32klatency 50ms
# apply tenant ipset
sudo iptables -A OUTPUT -m set --match-set vision_inc src -j CLASSIFY --set 10
```

jason: if policer helps, we should still run a canary dedicated slice for a weekend to verify no hidden regression (KV cache warmup differences).

lee: finance ok with a short-term canary if we provide cost/impact estimate first. please add expected $ range and retention.

anya: I'll prepare a routing rule PR for fallback to v2-quantized + update evals to make sure quality stays acceptable. low-risk: only trigger for export endpoints.

miguel: policer applied to rack-22 at 03:52 UTC. monitoring flagged within 2min, I'll post graphs in 5.

alloc-bot: Probe: qdisc applied -> observed egress reduction from 420MB/s -> 180MB/s on host eu-west-1b-rack-22 at 1746789130

sarah: initial numbers look promising — 95p dropped to ~230ms during the last two bursts. please keep monitoring for next 30m. if stable, we can draft the cost vs carveout doc and threshold for automation. :thumbsup:

miguel: leaving policer in place for now, will roll back if we see side-effects. noted potential for increased CPU due to tc overhead but negligible so far.

jason: next steps action list:
- Anya: PR for fallback routing to v2-quantized (scope: export endpoints)
- Lee: cost model for 8-slice carveout (include 1-week canary run)
- Miguel: validate policer across sibling racks (eu-west-1a/1c)
- Sarah: keep monitoring & capture request traces for any correctness regressions

sarah: copying in support to notify vision-inc about temporary shaping and offer canary dedicated slice (they might prefer a dedicated SLA).

lee: thanks all. i'll queue the budget ask if metrics hold.

anya: PR draft by EOD. will add automated rollback if quality drop >1% top-level metric.

miguel: updating runbook with NIC shaping steps and iptables snippet. logging everything in the incident ticket #INC-4521.

sarah: closing loop here in 1hr with final recommendation. great coordinated response. :white_check_mark:
